narrative.overview: Trace Desk is an evidence-led enterprise workspace, not a promotional crypto dashboard. A graphite and navy application shell holds a light slate work surface where scope, evidence, interpretation, and limitations remain visibly distinct. The visual system is compact, sober, and operational. Square-edged work areas, quiet rules, tabular numerals, and one teal interaction color let the case itself carry the interface.
keyCharacteristics: Dark institutional shell over a light, high-legibility case surface
One teal interaction voice and one amber limitation voice
Compact square components with explicit state, scope, and provenance
Evidence-first layouts that pair actions with the information they affect
Honest prototype language that never implies production controls

rules.name: The Semantic Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal means interaction or confirmed state. Amber means limitation or attention. Red means an actionable error.

rules.name: The Evidence Type Rule
rules.body: Monospace signals literal evidence, never generic technical sophistication.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface earns elevation only when it must remain contextually above scrolling evidence.

dos: Keep scope, evidence, interpretation, and limitations visually distinct.
Keep current case source, subject, QC state, and portable-file state visible.
Pair every evidence filter with a readable status and clear action.
Preserve keyboard focus, reduced motion, text alternatives, table captions, and mobile evidence labels.
State file-based persistence and prototype control limits at the action they affect.
donts: Do not add gradients, glows, dotted technical textures, glass effects, or decorative status pills.
Do not imply autosave, authenticated reviewers, enforced separation of duties, wallet attribution, or automated compliance decisions.
Do not use color as the only graph or status cue.
Do not use rounded cards as the default page structure or nest cards inside cards.
Do not use monospace for ordinary headings, labels, or body copy.
Do not hide technical limits inside a footer or separate documentation page.
